l: prayer to God, the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni
s: A prayer offered by an elder or priest while kneeling with the church, addressed to God, the Eternal Father, in Jesus Christ’s name.
Wine is blessed and sanctified, then drunk in meetings to remember Jesus Christ and his blood shed for those who drink it.

l: souls (of those who drink the wine), The Book of Moroni
s: A group is to remember Jesus Christ, have God's Spirit with them, and drink blessed wine in remembrance of his blood.

Baptism is for accountable people who truly repent, bring forth worthy fruit, have broken hearts and contrite spirits, witness remission of sins, and determine to serve Christ to the end. It fulfills commandments; baptizing little children is solemn mockery before God and denies Christ’s mercies.

are_conducted_by church of Christ [after the manner of the workings of the Spirit] The church's meetings occur often for fasting, prayer, discussion about the welfare of souls, and partaking of bread and wine in remembrance of the Lord Jesus. They are conducted according to the workings and power of the Holy Ghost.

Mormon is a prophet and Moroni’s father, permitted by God to speak. He teaches people to discern good and evil by the light of Christ, seek every good thing, and develop faith, hope, and charity. He judges Christ’s peaceable followers by their conduct, writes and prays continually for Moroni, teaches against baptizing little children, and warns the Nephites to repent.

l: Spirit of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: The Spirit of Christ is given to every man, enabling children of men to know good from evil and recognize what invites goodness and belief in Christ.
The devil is God’s continual enemy, fighting against God, inviting and persuading people toward sin and evil and away from belief in Christ; it cannot persuade anyone to do good.

Angels minister to people according to Christ’s command, appearing to those with strong faith and godliness, calling repentance, fulfilling the Father’s covenants, and declaring Christ’s word to chosen vessels.

Hope requires faith and charity, comes through Christ’s atonement and resurrection unto eternal life, and is filled by the Holy Ghost through meekness and lowliness of heart. Required for salvation, it contrasts with despair, which comes because of iniquity.

Charity is the pure, everlasting love of Christ. It is patient, kind, humble, selfless, truthful, enduring, and unfailing, neither envious nor easily angered. It accompanies faith and hope; without it a person is nothing and cannot be saved, while those possessing it at the last day fare well.

l: good and evil, The Book of Moroni
s: can_be_judged_by Spirit of Christ [with a perfect knowledge] Good comes from God and evil comes from the devil. The Spirit of Christ provides a clear way to distinguish them, and people are warned not to judge good as evil or evil as good.

l: mighty miracles, The Book of Moroni
s: Miracles are continuing manifestations wrought by faith; they have not ceased, but unbelief causes their cessation.

l: covenants of the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni
s: The covenants of the Eternal Father made with the house of Israel are to be fulfilled.

l: atonement of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: The atonement of Christ answers the law’s ends, claims those with faith in Christ, and provides hope of resurrection to eternal life.

Resurrection, enabled through Christ’s atonement and power, raises people to eternal life through faith; it culminates as spirit and body reunite and people are brought forth triumphantly before Jehovah.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: More than four hundred and twenty years have passed since the sign was given of the coming of Christ.
requires faith [in the name of Jesus Christ] People are saved by faith in the name of Jesus Christ. Without faith, people would be as though no redemption had been made.

l: words of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: The words of Christ declare that if people have faith, they can do all things which are expedient unto Christ. Moroni says the words written by him will be declared at the bar of God.

l: little children, The Book of Moroni
s: Little children are whole and unable to sin, so they need neither repentance nor baptism. Alive in Jesus Christ from the foundation of the world, they are all alike and partake of salvation.

Those who do away with the things Moroni teaches and die do so in their sins and cannot be saved in the kingdom of God. Through the grace of God and the shedding of the blood of Christ, people may receive remission of their sins and become holy.

l: writer (the speaker), The Book of Moroni
s: A living man writes amid grievous war with the Lamanites. Unable to enforce commands among his increasingly perverse people, he continues laboring and fears their destruction, preserves sacred records for his son, prays for him, and trusts in Christ.
stirs_up Lamanites [continually to anger one with another] Satan continually stirs the people up to anger one with another.

l: our people, The Book of Moroni
s: The people are an unrepentant, violently wicked group who have lost love for one another and continually seek blood and revenge. Without fear, order, mercy, principle, or feeling, they imprison the daughters of the Lamanites in Moriantum, violate them, murder them cruelly, and devour their flesh as bravery. They carry away provisions from Sherrizah and cause women and children suffering across the land, and are expected to perish unless they return unto God.

contains widows and their daughters [many remain there] Sherrizah is a tower from which the Lamanites took many men, women, and children as prisoners. Widows and their daughters remain there, while provisions left behind by the Lamanites were carried away by the army of Zenephi, leaving them to wander for food. Many old women faint and die along the way.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Moroni
s: The writer says that he and his son have a labor to perform while in the tabernacle of clay so that they may conquer the enemy of all righteousness and rest their souls in the kingdom of God. The kingdom of God is the place in which people cannot be saved without charity, faith, and hope. Those who do evil and die in their sins cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.

l: sore battle with the Lamanites, The Book of Moroni
s: results_in loss of choice men [the opposing side does not conquer] The sore battle with the Lamanites was not conquered by the writer’s people. Archeantus, Luram, and Emron fell by the sword, and many choice men were lost.

l: destruction of the people, The Book of Moroni
s: is_expected_without repentance [unless the people return unto God] The writer fears that the Lamanites will destroy the people because they do not repent and are continually stirred up to anger. He says that the people must perish unless they repent and return unto God, and that their destruction may resemble that of the Jaredites.

l: sufferings of the people, The Book of Moroni
s: The sufferings of the people include captivity, starvation, killings, cruelty, and the abandonment of women, children, and old women. The writer says that the suffering of the women and children across the land exceeds everything that can be told or written.

l: blood and revenge, The Book of Moroni
s: is_sought_by our people [because of wilfulness of their hearts] The people have lost their love for one another and thirst continually after blood and revenge. Their wilfulness in seeking blood and revenge is compared to that of the Jaredites.

l: return of the people unto God, The Book of Moroni
s: is_required_to_avoid destruction of the people The writer hopes that his son may live to witness the return of the people unto God or their utter destruction. He states that the people must perish unless they repent and return unto God.

l: sufferings and death of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: are_intended_to_lift son [with mercy, long-suffering, and hope of glory] The writer asks that Christ’s sufferings and death, together with the showing of his body unto their fathers, his mercy and long-suffering, and the hope of his glory and eternal life, remain in his son’s mind forever.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Moroni
s: has covenants of the Eternal Father [made with it] The house of Israel is called to awake and arise from the dust, put on beautiful garments, strengthen its stakes, enlarge its borders, and receive fulfillment of the covenants of the Eternal Father.
Jerusalem is called to awake and arise from the dust and put on its beautiful garments.
Zion is addressed as the daughter of Zion and is called to put on beautiful garments, strengthen its stakes, and enlarge its borders forever.
contain words of Christ Moroni seals up the records after exhorting the Lamanites. Readers are asked to remember the Lord’s mercy and ponder the records in their hearts.

l: gifts of God, The Book of Moroni
s: The gifts of God are many, come from the same God, and are given by the Spirit of God to profit people. They include wisdom, knowledge, great faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, angels and ministering spirits, tongues, and interpretation of languages. Distributed individually according to the Spirit of Christ’s will, they continue as long as the world stands, except according to the unbelief of the children of men.

l: salvation in the kingdom of God, The Book of Moroni
s: Salvation in the kingdom of God requires charity, faith, and hope. Those without charity, faith, or hope cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.

causes gifts of God [the power and gifts of God being done away] Unbelief can cause the spiritual gifts and power of God to be done away among people. Spiritual gifts continue only according to the unbelief of the children of men.

l: power of God, The Book of Moroni
s: works_through gifts of God [among those who do good] The power of God is not to be denied, because God works by power according to the faith of the children of men. If a person does good, that person works by the power and gifts of God, and denying that power prevents perfection in Christ.

l: Spirit of God, The Book of Moroni
s: The Spirit of God manifests spiritual gifts unto men to profit them. Through it, different people receive wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, visions of angels and ministering spirits, tongues, and interpretation.

Truth is manifested by God through the power of the Holy Ghost to those who ask with a sincere heart, real intent, and faith in Christ. By the power of the Holy Ghost, people may know the truth of all things.

l: grace of God, The Book of Moroni
s: is_sufficient_for Lamanites [to be perfect in Christ] The grace of God is sufficient for those who deny themselves of all ungodliness and love God with all their might, mind, and strength. By that grace, they may be perfect and sanctified in Christ.

l: blood of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: provides remission of sins [through the covenant of the Father] The blood of Christ is shed in the covenant of the Father for the remission of sins. Through it, people may become holy and without spot.
army of the nations (mustered by the LORD)
the ascension of Christ into heaven
